one_liner: Ladybird's JavaScript engine: an assembly-generated bytecode interpreter that outscores an -Os Duktape build but trails QuickJS.
what_it_does: LibJS is the ECMAScript engine of the Ladybird browser (inherited from SerenityOS): parser and bytecode compiler, a bytecode interpreter, the LibGC garbage collector and the full built-in library, exposed through Ladybird's internal C++ API (JS::VM::create, JS::Realm, ExecutionContext, as used by Utilities/js.cpp) plus a C host-object ABI (HostObjectABI.h) that LibWeb uses for platform objects. It is not packaged separately; you build it from the Ladybird monorepo, and the benchmarked binary is the js REPL that Ladybird's CI publishes as an artifact. A Rust crate (libjs_rust) is linked in; per a February 2026 newsletter snippet (page not opened) it reimplements the front end with byte-identical bytecode.
how_it_is_fast: Since March 2026 (PR #8299, 'AsmInt') the interpreter handlers are written in Flap, a typed DSL (Interpreter/interpreter.flap) that the Rust tool flapc lowers through SSA and register allocation into x86-64 or aarch64 assembly at build time; the bytecode PC and register-file pointer stay in machine registers and dispatch goes through a jump table. Values are NaN-boxed, and property access uses shape-keyed inline caches on the fast path, with slow paths in C++ (SlowPaths.cpp). PR #8299 reports 1.13-1.45x aggregate over the earlier C++ computed-goto interpreter (Kraken, Octane, JetStream; first-party). The LibJS tree has no JavaScript JIT tier.
when_to_use: You need a BSD-2-Clause engine aiming at full spec conformance (per an April 2026 newsletter snippet, 97.8% of 53,207 imported test262 subtests) and can live with interpreter-only speed.
Your code already builds inside the Ladybird or SerenityOS library stack (AK, LibGC, LibCore), so the dependency cost is already paid.

Object-heavy or numeric scripts on x86-64 or aarch64 Linux/macOS where you would otherwise use a size-optimised Duktape: 1.4x the Duktape score on Ubuntu, 1.3x on macOS arm64, and ahead on 7 of 8 v8-v7 tests (Crypto 1025 vs 783).
Studying a modern DSL-generated assembly interpreter (Flap) as a design reference.
when_not_to_use: Size-constrained embedding: the js binary is 43.8 MB on Ubuntu and 40.2 MB on macOS, against about 1 MB for QuickJS and 370 KB for Duktape (Score/MB 15 vs 1190 and 1352).
CPUs other than x86-64 and aarch64: LibJS/CMakeLists.txt stops with FATAL_ERROR because the generated assembly interpreter is the only interpreter (no portable C++ fallback any more).
RegExp-heavy scripts: LibRegex scores 66 vs Duktape 129 and QuickJS 398 on Ubuntu (114 vs 244 and 502 on macOS).
When throughput matters more than conformance: QuickJS (1217 / 1761), Hermes 0.12.0 (1530 / 1233) and PrimJS (737 / 1694) all outscore it on Ubuntu / macOS in the same suite.
When you need a stable, versioned embedding API: no standalone release, the C++ API is internal and changes with master, and the browser itself is labelled pre-alpha.

integration.form: C++ library (ladybird_lib LibJS) built inside the Ladybird monorepo; no standalone package or release
integration.dependencies: AK, LibCore, LibCrypto, LibFileSystem, LibRegex, LibSyntax, LibTextCodec, LibGC, LibUnicode with ICU data, simdjson, and the libjs_rust Rust staticlib (num-bigint, indexmap, foldhash; iced-x86 or fARM64 per arch); flapc (Rust) runs at build time
integration.min_toolchain: Clang/clang++ with CMake, Ninja and vcpkg (CI uses the ladybird-ci:2026.08.28 container), plus a Rust toolchain supporting edition 2024 (Rust 1.85+)
integration.platforms: x86-64 and aarch64 only; Linux and macOS benchmarked (ubuntu-latest, macos-latest arm64), Windows build paths exist in CMake (COFF, clang_rt) but the suite has no Windows row
integration.thread_safety: Not documented for the VM; LibGC's Heap.cpp states the collector is single-threaded

gotchas: The baseline is weak: Duktape 2.99.99 is unreleased master built with Duktape's default Makefile (-Os -fomit-frame-pointer), while LibJS uses Ladybird's Distribution preset with clang; against release-grade small engines (QuickJS, PrimJS, Hermes) LibJS loses.

Rankings swing by platform in this suite: LibJS beats QuickJS-NG 0.17.0 on Ubuntu (691 vs 647) but not on macOS (1169 vs 1660), and njs 0.9.2 beats it on Ubuntu (721) but not on macOS (950); one run per engine per day on shared runners, so treat gaps under about 10% as noise.

The suite's wall-clock column is longer for LibJS than for Duktape despite the higher score (79 s vs 70 s Ubuntu, 53 s vs 46 s macOS); the score covers only the timed benchmark loops, not process startup or teardown.

The harness pulls the latest successful master CI artifact daily and leaves the version cell blank (getVersion returns '' for ladybird), so a given score cannot be tied to a commit; Flap interpreter assertions are compiled into every build type (--enable-assertions), so they are included in the numbers.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose LibJS over QuickJS or njs only when spec conformance, the BSD-2 licence and the Ladybird code base matter more than binary size, portability and speed; QuickJS is faster in this same suite at about 1/40 of the size and embeds as a small C library, and Duktape remains smaller with a stable C API.
verified_claims_summary: ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark's daily GitHub Actions run (results dated 2026-10-05) runs the eight v8-v7 tests once per engine on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest arm64 runners (CPU not stated): LibJS, from Ladybird's own CI build (Distribution preset, clang), scores 691 vs 489 for Duktape 2.99.99 built at -Os on Ubuntu (about 1.4x) and 1169 vs 905 on macOS arm64 (about 1.3x), while QuickJS 2026.06.04 scores 1217 and 1761.
status_note: Very active (66.4k stars, commits daily, last 2026-10-06) and BSD-2-Clause, but LibJS is reachable only as part of a pre-alpha browser monorepo with a heavy build (Clang, vcpkg, Rust), so treat it as a reference design or an option for Ladybird-based projects rather than a drop-in embeddable engine.
